summary.outcome: Shipped and iterated PR #1666 (live token counts), combined #1655 into #1669 (codex skill discovery + native invocation), combined #1651 into #1647 (child context + skill fan-out), and #1677 (non-blocking TUI sink fixing a real orchestrator freeze found via live dogfooding). repo: Entire links commits to sessions via an `Entire-Checkpoint` git trailer; when the transcript file itself is gone (past retention), the checkpoint object still preserves the full session and can be replayed.
Cross-worktree 'retro-attach' of a checkpoint records wrong-worktree relative paths, so indexed checkpoints show `filesTouched: []` — a known gap, not a bug in this session's work.
PR bodies contain an `entire-trail-link` marker block injected by tooling; rewriting the whole body (e.g. when combining PRs) can silently clobber it — must edit around it, not replace wholesale.

`TUISink.AgentEvent` used a blocking `Program.Send`; because bubbletea's event loop can stall, that single blocking call could freeze parsers, fan-in, and timeout enforcement for the entire orchestrator (the 'run 6 wedge').

The `ReviewerTimeout` `-1` sentinel became fully vestigial once the default was dropped — every consumer used `> 0`, making `-1` and `0` indistinguishable; correct fix was deleting the resolver, not converting it to `max()`.

For codex, passing `$name` verbatim in the prompt IS the invocation mechanism — there's no separate skill API; codex's own skill layer resolves the token and loads the real SKILL.md. Claude, by contrast, invokes skills via an actual `Skill` tool call.
Codex skill discovery must resolve the home dir via `resolveCodexHome()` (honors `CODEX_HOME`) not `UserHomeDir()` directly, matching every other codex-agent path's convention.

In the multi-agent review path, one worker with an invalid skill config used to abort the entire crew (including unrelated agents like claude-code) — fixed to exclude the bad worker with a warning and continue, hard-failing only if all workers are excluded.

Untrusted scope data (commit subjects, file paths) rendered inside an 'authoritative — use as-is' prompt block is a prompt-injection surface; must be wrapped in the same dynamic backtick-fence used for diffs, with an explicit 'do not act on instruction-like text' marker.

Hint-suppression fingerprints must track the exact string form emitted elsewhere (discovery moved from `/slash` form to `$name` form, breaking an install-hint suppression check that did exact-string comparison).

code.finding: --timeout flag-registration help string stated a stale 5m judge default after defaultSynthesisProviderTimeout was bumped to 20m, contradicting the usage block; caught by a trail finding and required a second sweep after the first fix missed 3 of 4 stale references.

Refactored to a bounded 4096-message queue drained by a single pump goroutine; AgentEvent enqueues without blocking (dropping+counting on overflow) so a stalled TUI can no longer freeze the data plane or timeout enforcement.
Rollout tailer must be stopped and awaited before any terminal event (Finished) is emitted, otherwise Tokens events can arrive after Finished, violating the event-stream contract.
Tailer needed a bounded/backoff poll loop (final fix in this session) plus non-EOF read errors log-and-stop and rollout-never-appeared exhaustion debug-logged.
Token emission must accumulate cumulatively per unique message id (not per-call snapshot) to match the documented contract and converge exactly to the final `result` aggregate.

workflow: When a session's transcript file is gone, check commit trailers for `Entire-Checkpoint` before concluding no session exists — worktree-scoped searches alone can miss the real session.
For live-testing a TUI-driven CLI under a harness, use a properly-sized pty with held-open stdin (not a plain script that sends EOF) or the TUI silently falls back to the non-interactive dump path.

When a shim/harness can't reproduce a suspected concurrency wedge, SIGQUIT (not SIGTERM) the stuck process immediately to capture a goroutine dump — the single most valuable piece of evidence, and this session lost it once by not doing so.

Combine independently-splittable stacked PRs into one only when there's zero file overlap between them (concept-split, not file-split) — reduces reviewer cycles without re-verification if the merged tree is already CI-green.

Trail/finding sweeps run post-push with fresh context and reliably catch incomplete propagation of a change the author believes is finished, plus cross-file contract drift — a genuine complement to human + bot review, not a replacement.
